lines: 给一条鱼做动画，最经典的办法是骨骼：|六十到一百个关节，想怎么动就怎么动。
The classic way to animate a fish is a skeleton:|sixty to a hundred joints, and it can do anything you like.
可《ABZÛ》要的，是这样的画面。
But ABZÛ wanted something like this.

credit: GDC 2017 · Matt Nava · Creating the Art of ABZÛ
lines: 你看角落这里，我想大概有一万一千条鱼
you can see in the corner there, I think it's about 11,000 fish or something.
这些是巨大的鲹鱼
These are giant trevallies,
它们同时在游，每一条的节奏都不一样
and they all are swimming with a unique timing of their swim cycle at the same time.

credit: GDC 2017 · Matt Nava · Creating the Art of ABZÛ
lines: 我们试过用带骨骼的鱼来做这个场景
when we tried to do this scene with skeleton fish,
屏幕上大概只能放 30 条鱼
we only could get like 30 fish on the screen.
所以差别非常大
So it's a huge difference.
三十条，到一万一千条。|这一期，我们拆开《ABZÛ》的鱼。
Thirty fish, versus eleven thousand.|This episode, we take ABZÛ's fish apart.
骨骼动画贵在哪？|每一帧，每个关节都要算一次变换，|再把每个顶点按权重蒙到骨头上。
Why are skeletons expensive?|Every frame, every joint needs its transform computed,|and every vertex is skinned to its bones by weight.
一万条鱼乘一百个关节，就是一百万个关节，|每秒还要再算六十遍。
Ten thousand fish times a hundred joints is a million joints,|sixty times a second.
所以他们干脆把骨骼拿掉了。
So they took the skeletons away.
所有鱼共用一个静态网格，|用实例化一次画出成千上万份。
Every fish shares one static mesh,|drawn thousands of times in a single instanced call.
这项技术原本多用来画草地；|每个实例只带一小份数据。
The technique is usually used for grass;|each instance carries only a tiny bit of data.
在这期的演示里，每条鱼只有三十二个字节：|位置、相位、速度和转向。
In this demo, each fish is just thirty-two bytes:|position, phase, velocity and turn rate.
没有骨骼，鱼怎么动？|答案是在材质里直接挪顶点。
Without bones, how does a fish move?|By moving its vertices right in the material.
第一层，整条鱼左右平移；|第二层，绕中心点偏航。
Layer one: the whole fish slides side to side.|Layer two: it yaws around its center.
第三层，一道正弦波沿着脊椎传向尾巴；|第四层，身体沿脊椎扭转。
Layer three: a sine wave travels down the spine to the tail.|Layer four: the body twists along the spine.
再加一张蒙板，只让后半身摆动，|一条会游的鱼就出来了，一根骨头都没用。
Add a mask so only the back half swings,|and you have a swimming fish without a single bone.
四层动作都由同一个相位驱动。|每条鱼起始相位不同，鱼群就不会整齐划一。
All four layers run off a single phase.|Give every fish its own starting phase, and the school stops marching in lockstep.
相位的快慢跟着游速走：|加速时尾巴摆得又快又猛，然后滑行。
The phase speeds up with swim speed:|when a fish accelerates its tail beats hard, then it coasts.
咬合很难用正弦波做出来，|于是他们改用混合变形：
A bite is hard to make out of sine waves,|so they switched to blendshapes:
先张嘴，再把头往前送，同时合上嘴。
open the mouth, then thrust the head forward while it snaps shut.
螃蟹的腿也是四个混合姿态；|要用骨骼，一只螃蟹就得四十一个关节。
A crab's legs are four blended poses too;|with a skeleton, one crab would need forty-one joints.
鱼越长，问题越明显：|鲨鱼急转弯时，像一块木板在转。
The longer the fish, the worse it looks:|a shark in a hard turn rotates like a plank.
他们给鲨鱼做了四个卷曲姿态，|按转弯的方向和力度在中间插值。
They gave the shark four curl poses,|blended by the direction and strength of the turn.
可混合变形是叠加的：|向左和向上同时卷，尾巴就被拉得太远。
But blendshapes add up:|curl left and up at once, and the tail is pulled much too far.
最后只好再加一个专门的斜向姿态，把尾巴拉回来。
So they added one more pose just for the diagonal, to pull the tail back.
至于每条鱼往哪儿游，就交给上一期的群体规则：|位置和速度存在纹理里，在 GPU 上更新。
Where each fish swims comes from last episode's flocking rules:|positions and velocities live in textures and update on the GPU.
七种鱼，七次绘制调用，一万零二百四十条鱼，|每一条都按自己的节奏在游。
Seven species, seven draw calls, ten thousand two hundred forty fish,|each swimming to its own rhythm.
每条鱼，就是一小份数据，|加上一段所有鱼共用的代码。
Every fish is a tiny bit of data,|plus one piece of code that all fish share.
把这个想法推广到游戏里的每一个对象，|就是下一期的主角：ECS。
Apply that idea to every object in a game,|and you get the star of the next episode: ECS.
下一期：从《守望先锋》到《僵尸世界大战》。
Next time: from Overwatch to World War Z.
而这一切，还得从一条鱼说起。
And all of it starts, once again, with a single fish.
